title: Ekaterina Boyarkina
text:
Expertise




Machine Learning
I train and evaluate models on image and tabular data, from logistic regression to CNNs and pretrained ResNet-18. I have taken projects from preprocessing and EDA through to model evaluation.
Tech stack: Python PyTorch scikit-learn pandas NumPy Matplotlib seaborn XGBoost Hugging Face Weights & Biases Git





Robustness and Explainability
I test how models fail under FGSM attacks, and I compare defenses such as adversarial training. I have also used SHAP, LIME, and counterfactuals to explain cardiovascular risk predictions.
Methods: FGSM PGD Adversarial training Regularization SHAP LIME Counterfactuals





Data Engineering
In clinical data management, I independently designed and built a Python app to automate eTMF maintenance. In a team project, we built a citation data crawler and ran PageRank on a supercomputer, on a graph with millions of nodes.
Tech stack: SQL PostgreSQL Redis FastAPI Docker SLURM graph-tool NetworkX AWS pytest

title: Ekaterina Boyarkina
text:
Projects


Adversarial Robustness of Neural Networks
Started as my bachelor thesis, then became a tested Python package. Compares FGSM and PGD attacks, regularization, and adversarial training on logistic regression, CNNs, and ResNet-18. At ε = 0.15, adversarial training raised an MNIST CNN’s accuracy under PGD from 19.7% to 88.6%. Includes a FastAPI service and a live Gradio demo.
Python PyTorch FastAPI Gradio Docker pytest GitHub Actions Weights & Biases
Live demo


PageRank on Academic Citation Graphs
Crawled 50 million papers and 531 million references from the Semantic Scholar API, with a live dashboard to monitor progress. Computed PageRank on the FAU Erlangen-Nuremberg supercomputer and compared a custom NumPy implementation with NetworkX.
Python PostgreSQL Redis FastAPI graph-tool Docker SLURM


Explainable AI for Cardiovascular Risk Prediction
Student research project. Trains classifiers to predict cardiovascular disease risk, then explains the predictions with SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual explanations.
Python scikit-learn pandas SHAP LIME


Mushroom Edibility Classifier
Compares machine learning models that predict whether a mushroom is poisonous or edible, on a Kaggle dataset with 54,035 instances and 9 features.
Python Jupyter
